01 / DESIGN INTENT

Poised between
ground and sky.

AEROVANE V4 is a two-seat capsule and four-pod propulsion study. A pointed central body, continuous dark canopy and exposed triangulated links establish its mechanical character. Four independent fairings give the concept a broad, planted stance.

The name combines the ambition of air mobility with the directionality of a vane. Its emblem arranges four pods around a V-shaped central keel. Pearl shells, dark structure and satin rotor details make the visual systems legible.

Adapted from the supplied AEROVANE V4 Design Dossier. Reference renderings express design intent; they are not measured or validated engineering specifications.

02 / FORM & ASSEMBLY

Four stations.
One fluid form.

A faceted central shell narrows into a pointed nose. Rounded pod fairings contrast with angular body panels, while exposed connecting links give depth and structure to the silhouette.

The dossier describes a conceptual breakdown into a main framework, four pod housings and a fan system. The current supplied GLB is a single mesh with a shared material; it is presented intact, without reconstructed moving parts.

03 / CABIN & STRUCTURE

A human centre.
An exposed mechanism.

The cabin reference shows two seats, split instrument consoles and a lifting canopy. Triangulated links bridge the central body and outboard pods, bringing the mechanical architecture into view.

The dossier proposes composite fairings over a load-bearing chassis, metallic attachment points and electric drive. These are development directions. Canopy hinges, emergency egress, rotor containment and landing loads remain engineering work.

04 / PROPORTIONS

Scale as a
design assumption.

The dossier assumes a 4.80 m overall length. Width and height are derived from the study mesh proportions, with an approximate 0.66 m fan diameter. These figures describe the earlier proportion study; they are not surveyed dimensions of the uploaded model.

≈0.66 mFAN DIAMETER

05 / DEVELOPMENT STUDY

Compact disks.
A demanding brief.

The visible fan axes are lateral. This arrangement alone does not establish vertical lift. A tilting-pod system or a downward-flow architecture would need development before the flying-platform concept could be evaluated as an aircraft.

Electric drive, battery storage, inertial sensing and closed-loop control are technology categories identified in the dossier. Integration, cooling, fault tolerance and stability are unresolved for this design.

Explore the dossier’s illustrative sizing case

These are assumed inputs and first-order calculations from the supplied dossier, not vehicle performance specifications. The calculation assumes four vertically directed thrust disks, which the illustrated lateral-axis geometry does not provide.

Illustrative assumptions
Gross mass850 kg assumed
Motor budget4 × 200 kW peak candidate
Battery60–80 kWh candidate
Total disk areaApproximately 1.36 m²
Ideal hover powerApproximately 418 kW
Adjusted power estimateApproximately 699 kW before installation losses
Illustrative durationApproximately 4.1 minutes at 60 kWh and 80% usable energy, before reserves and auxiliary loads

Calculation basis: thrust T = mg; ideal power P = T3/2 / √(2ρA), using ρ = 1.225 kg/m³, a 0.65 figure of merit and 0.92 drive efficiency. Larger rotors or lower disk loading are alternatives for further study.

This is a sizing challenge, not evidence of flight capability. No endurance, structural or manufacturing certification is claimed.
